value: evening or nocturnal (most movement in evening or nocturnal diel periods)
method: radio-telemetry plus implanted tri-axial accelerometer data-loggers (1 Hz); random-forest classification of movement versus immobility, validated against field observations; activity budgets by diel period
conditions: Free-ranging adult male western diamond-backed rattlesnakes (males only; 12 of 19 implanted snakes analysed, the rest lost to device failures), Indio Mountains Research Station, Hudspeth County, Texas, June 2016 to August 2018 (median 35 days of data per snake, range 6-289). Diel periods defined as morning 0601-1000 h, diurnal 1001-1800 h, evening 1801-2100 h, nocturnal 2101-0600 h. Snakes located by radio telemetry at least twice weekly; no bait or lure mentioned; the paper does not say how the snakes were captured. The timing pattern was the same in all active seasons (spring, summer non-mating, summer mating, fall), but daily movement duration varied by season and increased in the summer mating season (next abstract sentence). Study is validation of a logging method; the species is highly sedentary.
